key_findings: The beta direct_billing tri-state is too coarse for Canadian extended-health workflows.
Electronic claim submission, provider payment assignment, payment recipient, predetermination, claim reversal and coordination of benefits are distinct capabilities.
TELUS eClaims is a major provider-side claims rail with insurer/provider-specific eligibility; public evidence reviewed does not establish a public consumer API for BenefitFlow.
Provider-directory evidence is discovery evidence only and cannot prove current direct-billing capability or member-plan coverage.
The current synthetic verifier must never infer direct billing merely from presence of an insurer name in production.
Production should separate provider capability confirmation from member-plan adjudication/predetermination and keep user cost estimated until plan-specific evidence exists.
recommended_primary_action: Harden ProviderVerification/direct-billing semantics before any live claims integration; then investigate sanctioned TELUS/insurer/practice-management integration pathways.
